Mr. M.C. Pant, learned counsel for

3. Counter affidavit has been filed by 
the respondents alongwith miscellaneous 
application (IA/1/2023).
4. Defect has been pointed out by the 
Registry of not filing a delay condonation 
application with the said counter affidavit.
5. In the opinion of this Court, this 
defect is trivial in nature and need not to 
consider. Therefore, the defect pointed 
out by the Registry is ruled out.
6. Counter affidavit filed by the 
respondents is taken on record.
Miscellaneous application made therefor 
stands disposed of.
7. Learned counsel for the petitioners 
prays for and is granted two weeks’ time 
for filing rejoinder affidavit.

said Committee to take a decision thereon.

learned counsel for the petitioner, list on 
15.04.2024, immediately after fresh cases.

Mr. M.C. Pant, learned counsel for 
petitioners.
2. Mr. Dinesh Gahatori, learned counsel 
for respondents/ONGC.
3. Learned counsel for the respondents 
submits that Tejbal and Rajesh Chawla 
have been entered in the service of ONGC 
at entry level E-1, therefore, the case of 
the petitioners is not similar to these two 
persons, and, accordingly, the same 
benefit could not be extended to the 
petitioners.
4. Learned counsel for the respondents
wants to bring this fact on record by way 
of filing a supplementary counter affidavit. 
Accordingly, four weeks’ time is granted to 
him to file the same.
5. List on 08.10.2024.
